message.content:
It’s hard to pick a single “best” film from 2020 because different people value different things—story, technical craft, cultural impact, box‑office success, etc. Below are a few titles that received widespread acclaim from critics, audiences, and award bodies during that year. (All of these were released in 2020; some were also contenders for awards in 2021.)

| Film | Director | Notable Accolades / Reception |
|------|----------|------------------------------|
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | 8.2 / 10 on IMDb, 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes; won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. |
| **Soul** | Pete Docter | 8.1 / 10 on IMDb, 95 % on Rotten Tomatoes; won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score. |
| **Tenet** | Christopher Nolan | 7.5 / 10 on IMDb, 70 % on Rotten Tomatoes; praised for its ambition and technical execution. |
| **The Father** | Florian Zeller | 7.9 / 10 on IMDb, 93 % on Rotten Tomatoes; won the Academy Award for Best Actor (Anthony Hopkins). |
| **Nomadland** | Chloé Zhao | 7.8 / 10 on IMDb, 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes; won the Academy Award for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actress (Frances McDormand). |
| **Minari** | Lee Isaac Chung | 7.9 / 10 on IMDb, 96 % on Rotten Tomatoes; praised for its heartfelt storytelling and cultural representation. |
| **Promising Young Woman** | Emerald Fennell | 7.5 / 10 on IMDb, 88 % on Rotten Tomatoes; won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. |

If you have a particular genre, theme, or metric in mind (e.g., box‑office gross, critical consensus, audience score), let me know and I can narrow the list further.
